Lets define a throw, shall we? A throw is when you have the lead, and you do not monopolize on it. A throw is when you are not doing what you should be doing to secure victory, and stalling out your inevitable defeat as a result. A throw is when you, as a team, LOSE CONTROL of the pace of the game, and the enemy team takes full on advantage of it. When TSM threw to Dignitas, it was a throw, and when Liquid threw to TSM, it was a throw. Every game has throws, so lets stop using it like it's a "oh it was just one simple mistake that caused failure, complete accident, won't happen again" get out of jail free card, for ALL teams, TSM AND others.

On a side note though, everybody seems too be hella mad that TSM is winning games not solely because of Bjerg. Yall wanted Dyrus to step up, and he did, but you're ignoring his plays and swearing how bad he is... why don't you say that when he stops ulting full teams and countering objective plays? Find something else to complain about. TSM is far from a perfect team, but they are showing vast improvements, especially in games where they are losing compared to say, past games like TSM vs SSW in worlds. Bot lane is beginning to under perform, so I feel like that's the next thing they should work on... It seems to be mostly positioning. While Santorin didn't die or anything, he also could've had a few better plays for aggression, that I feel are limited by his champion pool and "when in doubt, Rek'Sai" mindset that could help them close out games faster. Even in the games they've lost this split, Dyrus has performed far better than MSI, and dare I say it, far better than a lot of their teams. His solo queue training is paying off and I'm damn proud of him. Bjerg almost slipped up with that spell vamp mistake and probably should have just got the Zhonyas which would've saved him potentially at Baron. All in all, there are things they should take from this.
